name: Andrew Cherenson
why_notable: Wrote nslookup as a class project at UC Berkeley in 1986, while DNS was still replacing the HOSTS.TXT file. It first shipped in 4.3-Tahoe BSD and was carried into BIND, where it became the first widely available interactive tool for querying a name server directly and reading its raw answers. Microsoft and ReactOS later wrote their own versions of it. ISC's attempt to deprecate it in BIND 9 was reversed in 2004, and the tool still ships on almost every Unix, macOS and Windows system about forty years later.
